clue.text: Direct a girl to be perfectly honest

parts.note: direct means straight, as in a straight answer
Sadie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone tells a young woman she must always be completely truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct a girl' looks like an instruction to guide her somewhere; it is the adjective DIRECT plus A plus the name SADIE, with 'to be' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone utterly upright and truthful is said to be as straight as a die, a die being true on every face.

clue.text: Essays about old plays

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, so the attempts enclose the old

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, so essays are tries
old means aged

explanation.surface: Some school compositions discuss dramas from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' suggests compositions, but here it is the old sense of attempts; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragedies are serious dramas ending in disaster, a kind of stage work.

clue.text: A laundry is flooded

parts.note: laundry, the clothes to be cleaned, is the wash

explanation.surface: A launderette has its floor under water.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something awash is covered or swamped with water.

clue.text: Fashion model glad to get first prize

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A happy catwalk model wins the top award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the model's trade, but as a verb it tells you to rearrange MODEL GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Winners of Olympic and similar contests receive a gold award for first place.

clue.text: Trojan leader climbing mountain with poet

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Trojan
in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the mountain's name goes in backwards

parts.note: Ossa is a mountain in Greece, of the Pelion and Ossa legend

explanation.surface: A Trojan commander scales a peak alongside a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses OSSA to ASSO under the T of Trojan.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: One coming in to oust humble petitioner

indicators.note: coming in says the one enters the other word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: to oust is to supplant, to displace someone
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives to unseat a lowly person begging a favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One coming in' reads as a newcomer; it is I going inside SUPPLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant is one who begs humbly, a petitioner on bended knee.

clue.text: European heard to condescend

indicators.note: heard says the word is to be taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

explanation.surface: A continental is overheard being patronising.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one thinks beneath oneself.

clue.text: Soon given new role in English

indicators.note: in says the rearranged role sits within the abbreviation for English
new says the letters of role are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Before long, an actor gets a different part in an English production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the four letters of the part, and 'in' places the result after the first letter of the English abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb: before long, shortly.

clue.text: Artist displaying a little bed surrounded by ends?

indicators.note: surrounded by says the bit of bed sits inside the other word

parts.note: stubs are the ends left after a cigarette or pencil is used up

indicators.note: a little of a word is just its first letter, here of bed

explanation.surface: A painter shows a small bed hemmed in by leftover bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little bed' gives B, put inside STUBS; the question mark flags ends as stubs.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an English painter famous for horses.

clue.text: Topping item, always resplendent adorning heads

definitions.text: Topping item, always resplendent adorning heads

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of the preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: A crowning piece that always shines on top of royal heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headpiece, a topping worn on the head that shines.

clue.text: Cock-and-bull story about revised script? It may be discounted

indicators.note: about says the false story is wrapped round the reworked script

parts.note: a cock-and-bull story is an untrue tale, a lie

indicators.note: revised says the letters of script are reordered

explanation.surface: A fanciful tale wraps a rewritten screenplay, which may be marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the script, and 'about' wraps the false story round it; the question mark flags the price as the thing discounted.
explanation.definitionFit: The list price is the advertised retail figure, from which sellers often give reductions.

clue.text: Conductor seen in the morning behind a tree

indicators.note: behind says the morning comes after the tree

parts.note: a beech is a tree
a.m. stands for the morning

explanation.surface: A maestro is spotted early in the day behind a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated English orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Gibbons in Florida?

parts.note: apes in Florida suggests zoo animals, but Gibbons is the Tudor composer, whose first name matches a Florida city

explanation.surface: Are there apes living in the Sunshine State?
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbons is not the ape but Orlando Gibbons, the English Renaissance composer; his forename is also a city in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's forename doubles as the name of a city in central Florida.

clue.text: Shoot a descendant

definitions.meaning: a young plant shoot or cutting used for grafting
an heir or offspring of a family

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cutting taken for grafting, and an heir of a noble line.

clue.text: Dismembered — no wing, ear or tongue

indicators.note: dismembered means torn limb from limb, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mutilated body lacking a wing, an ear or a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismembered' rearranges NO WING EAR; tongue is the definition, in its sense of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and Norwegian is the language of Norway.

clue.text: Chow chow chow?

parts.note: chow is a breed of dog and also a verb for eating, so the three words read ...

explanation.surface: A repeated word that sounds like a call to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the words as a breed of dog, the slang verb to eat, then the dog again; the phrase means ruthlessly competitive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a ruthless, cut-throat contest where everyone fights for themselves.

clue.text: Reckless lady urged cautiously

indicators.note: reckless means wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A careless woman pushed someone to proceed carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reckless' rearranges LADY URGED.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: done in a careful, wary manner.

clue.text: Girl going to heart of Sussex to register as nonconformist

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: heart of means the middle letters of Sussex are taken

parts.note: to enter something is to register it, as on a list

explanation.surface: A woman travels to the middle of Sussex to sign up as a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSSEX is an English county; its middle letters are SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter is a Protestant who broke from the Church of England, a nonconformist.

clue.text: Alabama is in one country or another

indicators.note: is in says the state abbreviation sits inside the country

parts.note: Austria is a country
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Alabama belongs to some nation or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one country' looks like the definition, but it gives the wordplay; 'another' is the definition, a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a further nation, a different one from Austria.

clue.text: Roman general with a firm hold on the borders of Phrygia

parts.note: a grip is a firm hold

indicators.note: borders of means the outside letters of Phrygia, its first and last

explanation.surface: A Roman commander has a strong grip on the frontier of Phrygia.
explanation.walkthrough: Phrygia was an ancient region of Asia Minor; its first and last letters are P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's leading military commander.

clue.text: Contraltos can take part in opera

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Low-voiced singers are able to perform in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera about a singer and a painter.

clue.text: Sweet T?

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter T comes right ...

explanation.surface: Is a pudding just the letter T?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives T, which is the letter after S; read as a word, that gives the British term for a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is British slang for dessert, the sweet course eaten after the main meal.

clue.text: Intend appearing in torn clothing

indicators.note: appearing in says the purpose word shows up inside the other

parts.note: rent, as a past participle, means torn
to intend is to aim

explanation.surface: A plan shows up in ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Perfect trader's profession

definitions.meaning: flawless, as good as can be
what a trader professes or declares

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a flawless model, and a merchant's declaration that he trades, written as one word.

clue.text: Contemptible person, we hear, being drawn

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a toad is slang for a loathsome person

explanation.surface: A loathsome type, it is said, is being pulled along.
explanation.definitionFit: Towed means pulled or hauled behind a vehicle.

clue.text: Face caught without a hint of expression, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: without means outside, so face and caught go round the hint

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock, and slang for a person's face
ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter, here of expression

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted with a blank, expressionless face, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The surface suggests a poker face; the hint of expression is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional form of a language, a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Director or school head absent

indicators.note: head absent says the first letter of the school's name is dropped

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A film director or the headmaster has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' suggests film; it is a pointer, an arrow. HARROW is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign that points the way, something that directs.

clue.text: Seen in advance -Preston's first football manager joining United

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Preston's is taken

parts.note: Don Revie managed Leeds United and England
united, as of a couple, means wed

explanation.surface: A football boss joining United was spotted early, after a start at Preston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' suggests a club, but it means married: WED. Don Revie was a famous English football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To preview is to view something before its general release.

clue.text: Turner going backwards and forwards

indicators.note: going backwards and forwards says the word reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A painter goes to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner; it is something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Roman construction wasn't routine

definitions.meaning: from the proverb Rome wasn't built in a day
normal and unremarkable, part of the job

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ordinary, part of normal work; the proverb says Rome was not built so quickly.
